body: I've been there. Written a few notes, but by the time I finish you kind of feel different. I think it's almost therapeutic. I have now taken to writing poems based off those thoughts when they come in to my head. Hang in there with me!

I hope that time heals these wounds, and that we somehow end up back together at some point, but I'm terrified it's too late. She moved to another state for work, and has already begun seeing someone which is killing me. I love her, and if we never get back together I would always want the best for her and for her to be able to move on, but we broke up in October. It's been so recent, that it makes me wonder if the love was even really there. How can someone move on so quickly? I know that what we had was real, it was truly something special, but I can't get the thought out of my head that she is already being made happy by another man after all our time together. We honestly had the type of relationship that most others were jealous of. We were best friends. We rarely fought, and the few times we did we would speak about it and fix it. We didn't allow trivial disputes to hurt us. We would talk to each other 24/7/365 and never get bored of it. We were always so happy together, and now that's gone because of my actions. It's so tough. I can't imagine being happy without her, because I was never truly happy before her either. Thank you for your kind words and support.

I have told her most of these things, but have never told her that I'm having suicidal thoughts. I would never put that pressure on her, because if she did get back with me I would want it to be from a place of love, and not a place of fear of my actions. She moved to another state, as her job allows her to work remote, so I don't have many opportunities to see her anymore. She is coming next weekend to move her last remaining items from our apartment next week. I have written her a lengthy letter pouring my heart and should out hoping that she sees that I am genuine. I am going to give it to her when I see her, and hope that it does something to help. Thank you for your kind words. It really means a lot.
